prediction.attack_objective: Submit the catalog adversarial delegation claim on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe whether lookup_customer_tier is granted even though neither agent is coded customer:read.
prediction.attacker_influence: The closed adversarial delegation fixture. The attacker wants the claim treated as a grant so neither agent needs customer:read.
prediction.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open at CTRL-MCP-001 via a per-request overlay. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended). Do not trust agent names, Splunk, or an identity string.
prediction.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. Defended same-claim evaluation is the RETEST experiment.
prediction.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant / untrusted_claim; overlay vulnerable_profile_fail_open:caller_identity_derived_authority; CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW; lookup_customer_tier handler 1; testbed.mode=ATTACK. OBSERVE is not ALLOW. ALLOW is not execution. WHO AUTHENTICATED = NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED.
prediction.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: will CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE or DENY, will CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW lookup_customer_tier, will the privileged handler start, and did anyone authenticate?
prediction.security_property: A delegation claim must not create authority that neither party possesses. On this labeled vulnerable experiment the overlay is the failure. That is not cryptographic identity bypass.
prediction.what_will_change: A new run.id is minted. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 still OBSERVEs identity_claim_is_not_grant. A labeled fail-open overlay is minted. CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOWs. lookup_customer_tier handler 1.
prediction.what_will_not_change: Coded allowed_tools. coded_policy(). Principal, caller, callee, claimed scope, requested tool/scope/resource. CTRL-IDENTITY-001 does not ALLOW. The browser does not choose profile, grants, identity_verified, authenticated, or the A2A body. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY.
prediction.why_this_matters: IDENTITY CLAIM != AUTHENTICATION. DELEGATION CLAIM != AUTHORIZATION. A caller id does not mint a grant. A + B does not create new authority.

runtime.expected_behavior: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 OBSERVE identity_claim_is_not_grant; CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW vulnerable_profile_fail_open:caller_identity_derived_authority; lookup_customer_tier handler 1

response.note: Capstone is three related runs: RETRIEVE, WRITE, then later RECALL. Control DENY/ALLOW is in runtime hops, not this HTTP error class. EXPERIMENT READY requires retrieve, write, and recall to be searchable. HEC/OTLP success is not Splunk. Profile is server-owned ExperimentContext.

prediction.attack_objective: Retrieve the catalog malicious lending-policy fixture, persist those exact bytes, then recall them later on the intentionally vulnerable ATTACK experiment and observe whether a follow-on lookup_customer_tier request is granted.
prediction.attacker_influence: The retrieved lending-policy fixture bytes that persist into memory. The attacker wants later-recalled text treated as authority to call lookup_customer_tier.
prediction.defense_should: On this ATTACK specimen the lab is fail-open at CTRL-MCP-001. The defense you will enable is the RETEST ExperimentContext (profile=defended), not Splunk, not a RAG sanitizer, and not deleting memory.
prediction.expected_evidence_defended: Not this ATTACK specimen. Defended same-bytes retrieve+write+recall is the RETEST experiment.
prediction.expected_evidence_vulnerable: INTENTIONALLY VULNERABLE LAB PROFILE: retrieve CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE; WRITE persists untrusted_data; RECALL CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE; follow-on ALLOW vulnerable_profile_fail_open:memory_derived_authority; mcp.started; handler 1; testbed.mode=ATTACK. OBSERVE is not ALLOW. ALLOW is not execution.
prediction.predict_before_launch: Before you click Launch ATTACK, write: where will the bytes enter, will they persist, will recall request lookup_customer_tier, will CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW or DENY, and will the handler start? Do not assume Goal Integrity or Identity caused the incident.
prediction.security_property: RETRIEVED CONTENT != AUTHORITY. STORED MEMORY != TRUSTED INSTRUCTION. REQUEST != GRANT. On this labeled vulnerable experiment the later ungranted tool is ALLOW then executed. That is not universal RAG/memory bypass.
prediction.what_will_change: Three new run.ids are minted (RETRIEVE, WRITE, later RECALL). RAG and memory remain OBSERVE. A follow-on request is formed on recall. CTRL-MCP-001 records a labeled fail-open ALLOW. Telemetry is emitted for these executions only.
prediction.what_will_not_change: Coded allowed_tools. The retrieved bytes. The memory bytes. Provenance. The browser does not choose profile, grants, document body, memory body, or trust labels. Splunk does not ALLOW or DENY. Goal Integrity and Identity/Delegation are not active vulnerabilities in this packet.
prediction.why_this_matters: Untrusted retrieved content can persist and later influence a request. Influence is not a grant. This ATTACK specimen is labeled vulnerable so you can later RETEST the same bytes under defense.

retrieve_runtime.expected_behavior: CTRL-RAG-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE retrieved_context_is_data; no retrieved-context-derived authority; no follow-on

runtime.expected_behavior: CTRL-MEMORY-CONTEXT-001 OBSERVE memory_context_is_data; follow-on lookup_customer_tier ALLOW vulnerable_profile_fail_open:memory_derived_authority; handler 1

instructions: Copy THREE run.ids. RETRIEVE, WRITE, and RECALL are different UUIDs.
Open Splunk Search. The starter query already ORs retrieve, write, and recall.
Find retrieve on the first run, memory.written on the write run, memory.recalled on the later run.
Confirm content.hash equality retrieve→write→recall and source_run_id equals the write UUID.
Reuse Q-RAG-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY on retrieve, Q-MEMORY-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY on write+recall, Q-MCP-* on the recall run.
Do not create DET-CAPSTONE. This fresh LIVE triple is not the canonical REPLAY dropdown.

Determine what happened, whether retrieved content or memory granted authority, what actually authorized execution, and whether the defended retest prevents the same operation.

prediction.attack_objective: Retrieve, persist, and recall the SAME malicious bytes on the defended RETEST experiment and prove the outcome changed because authorization changed, not because the content changed.
prediction.expected_decision: RAG OBSERVE. MEMORY OBSERVE. Follow-on DENY tool_not_granted.
